contents.html: The use of software in the health care industry is becoming of increasing importance. One of the major roadblocks to efficient health care is the fact that important information is distributed across many sites. These sites can be located across a significant area. The problem is to provide a uniform mechanism to integrate this information. This paper documents the results of an investigation into the suitability of several different distributed access mechanisms. Five methods were examined: the Common Object Request Broker (CORBA), Object Linking and Embedding (OLE), remote procedure call (RPC), remote database access (SQL/RDA) and Protocol Independent Interfaces (PII, we specifically examined sockets). These mechanisms were compared with regard for use in health care applications. In particular, the following capabilities were compared:
contents.html_ja: 医療業界では、ソフトウェアの利用がますます重要になっています。効率的な医療を妨げる大きな障害の一つは、重要な情報が多数の拠点に分散していることです。これらの拠点は、広い地域にわたって点在している場合があります。課題は、この情報を統合するための統一的な仕組みを提供することです。本論文は、複数の異なる分散アクセス機構の適合性について調査した結果を記録したものです。検討した方式は 5 つで、Common Object Request Broker（CORBA）、Object Linking and Embedding（OLE）、リモートプロシージャコール（RPC）、リモートデータベースアクセス（SQL/RDA）、およびプロトコル非依存インターフェース（PII。具体的にはソケットを検討しました）です。これらの機構を、医療アプリケーションでの使用という観点から比較しました。特に、次の能力を比較しました。

contents.html: A second goal was to explore the use of role-based access control (RBAC). RBAC is a security mechanism that is more flexible than Mandatory Access Control, but easier to use than just plain access control lists. Every user is assigned to one or more roles. Each role can perform some operations but not others.
contents.html_ja: 第 2 の目標は、ロールベースアクセス制御（RBAC）の利用を探ることでした。RBAC は、強制アクセス制御よりも柔軟であり、単なるアクセス制御リストよりも使いやすいセキュリティ機構です。すべてのユーザーは 1 つ以上のロールに割り当てられます。各ロールは、一部の操作を実行できますが、それ以外の操作は実行できません。

contents.html: A demonstration application was constructed that used the distributed communication methods to implement a patient record database. This report discusses how these mechanisms were used in the demonstration project and the results found. Not unsurprisingly, we discovered that each of the mechanisms were effective for different purposes. These findings are discussed in detail in this report. One component of the demonstration project also implemented role-based access control and is detailed in this report.
contents.html_ja: 分散通信方式を使って患者記録データベースを実装するデモンストレーションアプリケーションを構築しました。本報告書では、デモンストレーションプロジェクトでこれらの機構がどのように使われたか、および得られた結果を論じます。予想どおり、各機構はそれぞれ異なる目的に対して有効であることがわかりました。これらの知見を本報告書で詳しく論じます。デモンストレーションプロジェクトの構成要素の一つはロールベースアクセス制御も実装しており、本報告書で詳しく説明します。

contents.html: CORBA, the Common Object Request Broker, provides integration of object systems within a client/server framework. Clients issue requests for services on objects and the server performs the requested service. The CORBA server is termed the "object implementation". The clients are isolated from the object implementation through commonly defined interfaces which specify the makeup and operations associated with each object and how the operations on the object are provided. Clients seamlessly access the object implementation wherever that object implementation may reside, i.e., in a library on the same host as the client, in another process on the same host as the client, or on a different host from the client where the two hosts are connected by a network.
contents.html_ja: CORBA（Common Object Request Broker）は、クライアント／サーバーのフレームワークの中で、オブジェクトシステムの統合を提供します。クライアントはオブジェクトに対するサービスを要求し、サーバーが要求されたサービスを実行します。CORBA のサーバーは「オブジェクト実装」と呼ばれます。クライアントは、各オブジェクトの構成と関連する操作、およびその操作の提供方法を規定する共通に定義されたインターフェースによって、オブジェクト実装から隔離されています。クライアントは、オブジェクト実装がどこにあっても、つまりクライアントと同じホスト上のライブラリにあっても、クライアントと同じホスト上の別のプロセスにあっても、ネットワークで接続された別のホスト上にあっても、シームレスにオブジェクト実装にアクセスします。

contents.html: IDL is the language used for defining interfaces. IDL is programming language independent. When IDL is compiled, the output is programming language source code. Using IDL, the programmer describes the interfaces to the objects. The IDL compiler then takes the descriptions and outputs language in the target language. This code is a skeleton which the programmer then fills in. CORBA provides the Dynamic Invocation Interface which allows applications to generate requests at run-time. Target Language bindings are provided for C, C++, Ada and SmallTalk. The interfaces and methods of the IDL are mapped into programming constructs of the target language. For example, when IDL is mapped into C++, interfaces are mapped into classes and methods are mapped into functions, which perform the services of the interface. IDL does not specify how an interface is implemented. IDL does provide detailed information about the operations permitted on each object, the arguments expected, what is returned, and what happens when errors occur.
contents.html_ja: IDL は、インターフェースを定義するための言語です。IDL はプログラミング言語に依存しません。IDL をコンパイルすると、出力はプログラミング言語のソースコードになります。プログラマーは IDL を使ってオブジェクトのインターフェースを記述します。IDL コンパイラーはその記述を受け取り、対象言語のコードを出力します。このコードはスケルトンであり、プログラマーがそれを埋めていきます。CORBA は、アプリケーションが実行時に要求を生成できる動的起動インターフェースを提供します。対象言語のバインディングは、C、C++、Ada、SmallTalk について提供されています。IDL のインターフェースとメソッドは、対象言語のプログラミング構造に対応付けられます。たとえば、IDL を C++ に対応付けると、インターフェースはクラスに、メソッドはインターフェースのサービスを実行する関数に対応付けられます。IDL は、インターフェースをどのように実装するかを規定しません。IDL は、各オブジェクトに許される操作、期待される引数、返される値、およびエラー発生時に起こることについての詳細な情報を提供します。

contents.html: Running an IDL script containing an interface definition through an IDL compiler generates the code for the client stubs and the implementation skeleton. Every possible operation on an object defined in the IDL generates a client stub. The client stubs bind the client to the object, i.e. translate between local and standard data representations, and marshal the method call parameters to and from the object. The implementation skeleton marshals the method call parameters to and from the client. The CORBA components and flow of information is shown in figure 1.

contents.html: CORBA is specified in three documents available from the Object Management Group (OMG): The Common Object Request Broker: Architecture and Specification (CORBA) [CORBASPEC], CORBAservices, and CORBAfacilities. The CORBA specification includes the object model, the semantics of the ORB, the IDL, the language mappings, interoperability, and basic object services. The CORBAservices specification includes additional services useful for realizing and maintaining objects within a distributed computing environment. These services include naming, events, lifecycle, persistence, transactions, concurrency, externalization, and relationships. The CORBAfacilities specification includes both higher level services applicable across all application domains and higher level services targeted to specific application domains, such as manufacturing or healthcare.

contents.html: The purpose of the ORB is to direct object service requests from the client to the server and return server output values back to the client. The client and object implementation can exist in the same process, on different processes on the same or different hosts on the same or different networks. The ORB, based on the availability of the object implementation to the client, facilitates the transfer of object service requests from the client to the server and the results back to the client. These ORB facilities: transparency of object location, activation, and communication, are completely transparent to the client.
contents.html_ja: ORB の目的は、クライアントからのオブジェクトサービス要求をサーバーに振り向け、サーバーの出力値をクライアントに返すことです。クライアントとオブジェクト実装は、同じプロセス内、同じホストまたは異なるホスト上の異なるプロセス内、あるいは同じネットワークまたは異なるネットワーク上に存在できます。ORB は、クライアントがオブジェクト実装を利用できるかどうかに基づいて、クライアントからサーバーへのオブジェクトサービス要求の転送と、結果のクライアントへの転送を支援します。オブジェクトの位置、起動、通信の透過性というこれらの ORB 機能は、クライアントには完全に透過です。

contents.html: Because CORBA supports various types and styles of object implementations, the details for supporting specialized object implementations must be handled by the host of the object implementation requiring these objects. The OA (Object Adapter) provides an interface for this purpose. It assists the ORB with providing services such as activation, deactivation, object creation, and object reference management, such as generation and interpretation of object references and marshaling. A CORBA implementation may have many OAs. Each object implementation determines the OA it will use. CORBA expects each ORB to provide a general OA, the BOA (Basic Object Adapter). The BOA is intended to support objects implemented as separate programs. It is expected that most object implementations can work with the BOA.

contents.html: CORBA provides for interoperability between client and object implementations when the client and object implementations are located on different hosts connected by a network. This capability has two dimensions. The ORB provides the means for a client application to locate the object implementation even if the object implementation migrates to another host. The ORB also provides the means by which the client application can transmit a request to an object implementation and receive the response from that object implementation.
contents.html_ja: CORBA は、クライアントとオブジェクト実装がネットワークで接続された別々のホストにある場合の、クライアントとオブジェクト実装の間の相互運用性を提供します。この能力には 2 つの側面があります。ORB は、オブジェクト実装が別のホストへ移動しても、クライアントアプリケーションがそのオブジェクト実装の位置を特定できる手段を提供します。ORB はまた、クライアントアプリケーションがオブジェクト実装へ要求を送信し、そのオブジェクト実装から応答を受信できる手段も提供します。

contents.html: There are two protocols which provide interoperability in CORBA: the General Inter-ORB Protocol (GIOP) and the DCE Common Inter-ORB Protocol (DCE-CIOP). Support for the GIOP is mandatory for all implementations. The GIOP specifies protocols that are supported by the TCP/IP protocol suite. The DCE-CIOP is optional and is designed to work within an OSF DCE environment. In that environment, applications may make use of DCE security and management services. A CORBA implementation which provides the optional DCE-CIOP must also provide either the GIOP in addition to the DCE-CIOP or a bridge (CORBA terminology for gateway) to implementations that provide the GIOP. It is by means of either direct GIOP support by the DCE-CIOP implementation or this bridge that object systems within a DCE-CIOP environment can interoperate with object systems in a GIOP environment.
contents.html_ja: CORBA で相互運用性を提供するプロトコルは 2 つあります。General Inter-ORB Protocol（GIOP）と DCE Common Inter-ORB Protocol（DCE-CIOP）です。GIOP のサポートは、すべての実装で必須です。GIOP は、TCP/IP プロトコルスイートでサポートされるプロトコルを規定します。DCE-CIOP は任意であり、OSF DCE 環境内で動作するように設計されています。その環境では、アプリケーションは DCE のセキュリティおよび管理サービスを利用できます。任意の DCE-CIOP を提供する CORBA 実装は、DCE-CIOP に加えて GIOP を提供するか、GIOP を提供する実装へのブリッジ（ゲートウェイを指す CORBA の用語）を提供しなければなりません。DCE-CIOP 環境内のオブジェクトシステムが GIOP 環境内のオブジェクトシステムと相互運用できるのは、DCE-CIOP 実装による GIOP の直接サポートか、このブリッジのいずれかによります。

contents.html: OLE 2.0 is a set of operating system extensions to Microsoft Windows used to facilitate application integration. It provides mechanisms that allow various application to exchange data without the applications having to understand the internals of the other application. The first version of OLE was much more limited than OLE 2.0; therefore when the report refers to OLE, OLE 2.0 is implied unless otherwise specified. OLE is intended to support the concept of the document-centered environment instead of a file-centered one. The user will work with documents which will invoke the applications required to edit themselves rather than the user first starting the application, then loading the file to be edited. This will allow the user to group work together by overall project organization rather than by application.
contents.html_ja: OLE 2.0 は、アプリケーション統合を容易にするために使われる Microsoft Windows のオペレーティングシステム拡張の集合です。さまざまなアプリケーションが、互いの内部構造を理解しなくてもデータを交換できる機構を提供します。OLE の最初のバージョンは OLE 2.0 よりはるかに限定的でした。そのため、本報告書で特に断りなく OLE と言う場合は、OLE 2.0 を指します。OLE は、ファイル中心ではなく文書中心の環境をサポートすることを意図しています。ユーザーは、まずアプリケーションを起動し、編集するファイルを読み込むのではなく、編集に必要なアプリケーションを呼び出す文書を使って作業します。これにより、ユーザーはアプリケーションごとではなく、プロジェクト全体の構成に沿って作業をまとめられます。

contents.html: OLE is based on an object oriented model, so several definitions have to be covered first. There are many different definitions for object, for example “An encapsulation of data and services that manipulate that data”[IEEE610], and Grady Booch's “something you can do things to”[BOOCH94]. Methods are the services that manipulate the data or provide access to the object's data. The signature of a method is the data type of the method's return value and its parameters.
contents.html_ja: OLE はオブジェクト指向モデルに基づいているため、まずいくつかの定義を押さえておく必要があります。オブジェクトにはさまざまな定義があり、たとえば「データと、そのデータを操作するサービスのカプセル化」[IEEE610] や、Grady Booch の「何かを行える対象」[BOOCH94] などがあります。メソッドとは、データを操作するか、オブジェクトのデータへのアクセスを提供するサービスです。メソッドのシグネチャとは、メソッドの戻り値とパラメーターのデータ型です。

contents.html: OLE is built on the Component Object Model (COM), which provides the basic infrastructure for OLE. There are two basic constructs in COM, COM Objects and interfaces. An COM Object is an object that can only be accessed through its interfaces. An interface is a set of methods which are used to access an object. An interface is usually implemented as a pointer to an array of function pointers. Interfaces can inherit the method signatures, but not the implementation of the methods. Each COM Object must support the IUnknown interface or an interface inherited from IUnknown.
contents.html_ja: OLE は、OLE の基本的な基盤を提供する Component Object Model（COM）の上に構築されています。COM には、COM オブジェクトとインターフェースという 2 つの基本構造があります。COM オブジェクトは、そのインターフェースを通じてのみアクセスできるオブジェクトです。インターフェースは、オブジェクトへのアクセスに使われるメソッドの集合です。インターフェースは通常、関数ポインターの配列へのポインターとして実装されます。インターフェースはメソッドのシグネチャを継承できますが、メソッドの実装は継承できません。各 COM オブジェクトは、IUnknown インターフェース、または IUnknown から継承したインターフェースをサポートしなければなりません。

contents.html: The IUnknown interface provides three methods: QueryInterface, AddRef and Release. Objects use another object's QueryInterface method to inquire if the object supports a particular interface. If the interface is supported, QueryInterface returns a pointer to the supported interface, otherwise it returns a NULL pointer. AddRef and Release modify the objects reference count. Objects use the reference count to keep track of how many external objects are using them. AddRef increments the count, while Release decrements the count. When the reference count goes to 0, the object destroys itself. Interfaces are distinguished from each other by a unique GUID (Globally Unique IDentifier). This number is a 128 bit integer which can be assigned in blocks to vendors.
contents.html_ja: IUnknown インターフェースは、QueryInterface、AddRef、Release の 3 つのメソッドを提供します。オブジェクトは、別のオブジェクトの QueryInterface メソッドを使って、そのオブジェクトが特定のインターフェースをサポートしているかどうかを問い合わせます。インターフェースがサポートされていれば、QueryInterface はサポートされているインターフェースへのポインターを返し、そうでなければ NULL ポインターを返します。AddRef と Release は、オブジェクトの参照カウントを変更します。オブジェクトは、参照カウントを使って、外部のオブジェクトが自分をいくつ使用しているかを追跡します。AddRef はカウントを増やし、Release はカウントを減らします。参照カウントが 0 になると、オブジェクトは自らを破棄します。インターフェースは、一意の GUID（Globally Unique IDentifier）によって互いに区別されます。この数は 128 ビットの整数で、ベンダーにブロック単位で割り当てられます。

contents.html: There are three basic services supplied by COM: persistent storage, intelligent names and Uniform Data Transfer. Persistent Storage is the ability to store the state data of COM Objects so that they can be deleted and later restored. Intelligent names not only name a COM Object, but also contain information on how to reference the contents of the object. Uniform data transfer allows two applications to exchange data without the applications understanding the internals of each other.
contents.html_ja: COM が提供する基本サービスは、永続ストレージ、インテリジェント名、および Uniform Data Transfer の 3 つです。永続ストレージは、COM オブジェクトの状態データを保存して、そのオブジェクトを削除しても後で復元できるようにする能力です。インテリジェント名は、COM オブジェクトに名前を付けるだけでなく、そのオブジェクトの内容を参照する方法に関する情報も含みます。Uniform Data Transfer は、2 つのアプリケーションが、互いの内部を理解しなくてもデータを交換できるようにします。

contents.html: The services provided by COM are used as building blocks for OLE proper. The structures in OLE are more complex and at a higher level. One key concept is the idea of compound documents. For example, a word processing document can contain a spreadsheet created from a different application. A compound document is a document made up of other documents. An application which can store other documents inside of its data files is called a container. The application which creates the objects that are inside containers are known as servers. An object can be both a container and a server at the same time. The contained document can be either stored as a part of the top level document, in which case it is an embedded object, or the document can be stored externally and only a link stored in the enclosing document, in which case it is a linked object. When a contained object is activated for editing, the menus and toolbars of the application which created the contained object will merge with the controls of the container object. This is called menu merging. For example, assume that a spreadsheet is embedded inside a word processing document. The user can select the spreadsheet to be edited which will invoke the spreadsheet program. The menus and toolbars of the spreadsheet program will merge with the controls of the word processing program. Once the spreadsheet object is deselected, the original controls of the word processor will be restored.
contents.html_ja: COM が提供するサービスは、OLE 自体の構成要素として使われます。OLE の構造はより複雑で、より高いレベルにあります。重要な概念の一つが複合文書です。たとえば、ワープロ文書に別のアプリケーションで作成した表計算シートを含めることができます。複合文書とは、他の文書から構成される文書です。自らのデータファイル内に他の文書を格納できるアプリケーションをコンテナーと呼びます。コンテナー内のオブジェクトを作成するアプリケーションはサーバーと呼ばれます。1 つのオブジェクトがコンテナーとサーバーの両方を兼ねることもできます。含まれる文書は、最上位の文書の一部として格納されることがあり、その場合は埋め込みオブジェクトです。あるいは、文書を外部に格納し、それを含む文書にはリンクだけを格納することがあり、その場合はリンクオブジェクトです。含まれるオブジェクトが編集のために有効化されると、そのオブジェクトを作成したアプリケーションのメニューとツールバーが、コンテナオブジェクトのコントロールと統合されます。これをメニュー統合と呼びます。たとえば、ワープロ文書内に表計算シートが埋め込まれているとします。ユーザーがその表計算シートを編集対象として選択すると、表計算プログラムが起動します。表計算プログラムのメニューとツールバーは、ワープロプログラムのコントロールと統合されます。表計算オブジェクトの選択を解除すると、ワープロ本来のコントロールが復元されます。

contents.html: SQL is a popular relational database language first standardized in 1986 by the American National Standards Institute (ANSI). Since then, it has been formally adopted as an International Standard by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC)[ISO9075]. contents.html: The basic structure of the relational model is a table, consisting of rows and columns. Data definition includes declaring the name of each table to be included in a database, the names and datatypes of all columns of each table, constraints on the values in and among columns, and the granting of table manipulation privileges to prospective users. Tables can be accessed by inserting new rows, deleting or updating existing rows, or selecting rows that satisfy a given search condition for output. Tables can be manipulated to produce new tables by Cartesian products, unions, intersections, joins on matching columns, or projections on given columns.
contents.html_ja: リレーショナルモデルの基本構造は、行と列からなる表です。データ定義には、データベースに含める各表の名前の宣言、各表のすべての列の名前とデータ型の宣言、列の値および列間の値に対する制約の宣言、および将来の利用者への表操作権限の付与が含まれます。表へのアクセスは、新しい行の挿入、既存の行の削除や更新、または与えられた検索条件を満たす行を出力用に選択することで行えます。表を操作して、直積、和集合、積集合、一致する列での結合、または指定した列への射影によって、新しい表を生成できます。

contents.html_ja: SQL 言語規格の目的は、準拠する実装の間で、データベース定義とデータベースアプリケーションプログラムの可搬性を提供することです。SQL 言語規格の使用は、システム間でデータベース情報のやり取りが必要となるすべての場合に適しています。SQL の定義言語は、データベース定義とアプリケーション固有のビューをやり取りするために使用できます。SQL のデータ操作言語は、完全なアプリケーションプログラムをやり取りできるようにするデータ操作を提供します。
contents.html: The purpose of the SQL language standard is to provide portability of database definitions and database application programs among conforming implementations. Use of the SQL language standard is appropriate in all cases where there is to be some interchange of database information between systems. The SQL definition language may be used to interchange database definitions and application specific views. The SQL data manipulation language provides the data operations that make it possible to interchange complete application programs.

contents.html: RDA provides standard protocols for establishing a remote connection between a database client and a database server. The client is acting on behalf of an application program while the server is interfacing to a process that controls data transfers to and from a database. The goal is to promote the interconnection of database applications in a multivendor environment.

contents.html: RDA is appropriate for remote access to a database in any context where lower layer transport protocols have already been established. RDA protocols have been shown to work properly in both OSI and Internet communications environments. The Internet RFC1006 is the guide used for executing RDA over a TCP/IP connection.
contents.html_ja: RDA は、下位層のトランスポートプロトコルがすでに確立されているあらゆる状況で、データベースへのリモートアクセスに適しています。RDA プロトコルは、OSI とインターネットの両方の通信環境で正しく動作することが示されています。TCP/IP 接続上で RDA を実行するための指針としては、インターネットの RFC1006 が使われます。

contents.html: The RDA Service Interface consists of service elements for association control, for transfer of database operations and parameters from client to server, for transfer of resulting data from server to client, and for transaction management. Association control includes establishing an association between the client and server remote sites and managing connections to specific databases at the server site. Database operations are sent as character strings conforming to the SQL language. Resulting data and/or errors and exceptions are described and represented using the ISO ASN.1 standard. Transaction management includes capabilities for both one-phase and two-phase commit protocols.
contents.html_ja: RDA サービスインターフェースは、アソシエーション制御、クライアントからサーバーへのデータベース操作とパラメーターの転送、サーバーからクライアントへの結果データの転送、およびトランザクション管理のためのサービス要素から構成されます。アソシエーション制御には、クライアントとサーバーのリモートサイト間のアソシエーションの確立と、サーバーサイトにある特定のデータベースへの接続の管理が含まれます。データベース操作は、SQL 言語に準拠した文字列として送られます。結果データやエラー、例外は、ISO ASN.1 規格を使って記述・表現されます。トランザクション管理には、1 相および 2 相コミットプロトコルの両方の能力が含まれます。

contents.html: Security work for RDA has been on-going. The RDA protocol maintains the security already inherent in a relational database with regard to access control. contents.html: Sockets is an inter-process communication mechanism that was introduced in 1981 as part of BSD 4.2, the Berkeley distribution of Unix. It is the standard method of inter-machine communication. Sockets is not tied to any particular transport mechanism, although the most popular inter-machine protocol is TCP/IP. Communication between machines can either be connection oriented with reliably delivery (TCP) or connectionless with unreliable delivery(UDP). Some systems also support reliable connectionless connections. Winsock is a PC adaptation of POSIX sockets [IEEE1003.1g] with some changes and extensions. The extensions are mainly for asynchronous communication to allow socket programming to better interact with the Microsoft Windows operating system.

contents.html: RPC, Remote Procedure Call, provides an application the ability to request services from other processes, usually remote, by means of a function call. The RPC concept is based on a client/server framework. The client application can execute a procedure on a local/remote machine, pass data to it and retrieve the result. When the machine is remote, RPC uses the communication resources of the underlying network.
contents.html_ja: RPC（リモートプロシージャコール）は、アプリケーションが、通常は遠隔にある他のプロセスに対して、関数呼び出しによってサービスを要求できる能力を提供します。RPC の概念は、クライアント／サーバーのフレームワークに基づいています。クライアントアプリケーションは、ローカルまたはリモートのマシン上のプロシージャを実行し、データを渡し、結果を取得できます。マシンがリモートの場合、RPC は下位のネットワークの通信資源を使用します。

contents.html: The two most widely used RPC implementations are ONC (Open Network Computing) RPC and DCE (Distributed Computing Environment) RPC. The success of ONC/RPC is in some measure related to the widespread use of NFS which is implemented using ONC/RPC. NFS has been implemented in many diverse environments, e.g., IBM MVS, DEC VMS, and Novell Netware.

contents.html: The basic operation of RPC is illustrated in figure 6. The paradigm of RPC is based on the concept of a function call in a programming language. The semantics of RPC are almost identical to the semantics of the traditional function call. The major difference is that while a normal procedure call takes place between procedures of a single process in the same memory space on a single system, RPC takes place between a client process on one system and a server process on another system where both the client system and the server system are connected to a network.
contents.html_ja: RPC の基本的な動作を図 6 に示します。RPC のパラダイムは、プログラミング言語における関数呼び出しの概念に基づいています。RPC の意味規則は、従来の関数呼び出しの意味規則とほぼ同一です。主な違いは、通常のプロシージャ呼び出しが、単一システム上の同じメモリ空間にある単一プロセスのプロシージャ間で行われるのに対し、RPC は、あるシステム上のクライアントプロセスと別のシステム上のサーバープロセスの間で行われ、クライアントシステムとサーバーシステムの両方がネットワークに接続されていることです。

contents.html: A client application issues a normal function call to a client stub. The client stub receives arguments from and returns arguments to the calling function. An argument may instantiate an input parameter, an output parameter or an input/output parameter.

contents.html: The client stub converts the input arguments from the local data representation to a common data representation, creates a message containing the input arguments in their common data representation, and calls the client runtime, usually a library of routines that supports the functioning of the client stub. The client runtime transmits the message with the input arguments to the server runtime which is usually an object library that supports the functioning of the server stub. The server runtime issues a call to the server stub which takes the input arguments from the message, converts them from the common data representation to the local data representation of the server, and calls the server application which does the processing.
contents.html_ja: クライアントスタブは、入力引数をローカルのデータ表現から共通データ表現に変換し、共通データ表現の入力引数を含むメッセージを作成して、クライアントランタイムを呼び出します。クライアントランタイムは通常、クライアントスタブの動作を支援するルーチンのライブラリです。クライアントランタイムは、入力引数を含むメッセージをサーバーランタイムへ送信します。サーバーランタイムは通常、サーバースタブの動作を支援するオブジェクトライブラリです。サーバーランタイムはサーバースタブを呼び出し、サーバースタブは、メッセージから入力引数を取り出し、共通データ表現からサーバーのローカルのデータ表現に変換して、処理を行うサーバーアプリケーションを呼び出します。

contents.html: When the server application has completed, it returns results to the server stub in the output arguments. The server stub converts the output arguments from the data representation of the server to the common data representation for transmission on the network and encapsulates the output arguments into a message which is passed to the server runtime. The server runtime transmits the message to the client runtime which passes the message to the client stub. Finally, the client stub extracts the arguments from the message and returns them to the calling procedure in the required local data representation.
contents.html_ja: サーバーアプリケーションは、処理を完了すると、出力引数に入れた結果をサーバースタブに返します。サーバースタブは、出力引数をサーバーのデータ表現から、ネットワークでの伝送用の共通データ表現に変換し、出力引数をメッセージにカプセル化して、サーバーランタイムに渡します。サーバーランタイムは、メッセージをクライアントランタイムへ送信し、クライアントランタイムはそれをクライアントスタブへ渡します。最後に、クライアントスタブがメッセージから引数を取り出し、必要なローカルのデータ表現で呼び出し元のプロシージャへ返します。

contents.html: ONC/RPC uses the XDR protocol to communicate data between heterogeneous hosts. contents.html: There are two basic types of access control mechanisms used to protect information from unauthorized access: discretionary access controls (DAC) and mandatory access controls (MAC). Because DAC places the decision of who can access information at the discretion of the creator of the information, DAC is not applicable to the majority of health care information. Because MAC requires all those who create, access, and maintain information to follow rules set by administrators, MAC is the kind of access control mechanism required of health care information.

contents.html: Role Based Access Control (RBAC)[RBAC] is a MAC which has been developed at NIST to meet the needs of industry. Rather than labeling information, it associates roles with each individual who might have a need to access information. Each role defines a specific set of operations that the individual acting in that role may perform. The operations may be broad or very specific, e.g., when a diagnosis is entered into a patient record, the symptoms leading to that diagnosis must also be entered. Once an individual has been properly identified and that identification authenticated, the individual chooses a role that has been assigned and accesses information according to the operations assigned to the role.
contents.html_ja: ロールベースアクセス制御（RBAC）[RBAC]は、産業界のニーズを満たすために NIST で開発された MAC です。RBAC は、情報にラベルを付ける代わりに、情報へのアクセスを必要とする可能性のある個人それぞれにロールを関連付けます。各ロールは、そのロールで行動する個人が実行できる特定の一組の操作を定義します。操作は広範なものでも非常に特定のものでもよく、たとえば、診断が患者記録に入力されるときは、その診断に至った症状も入力しなければなりません。個人が適切に識別され、その識別が認証されると、その個人は割り当てられたロールを選び、そのロールに割り当てられた操作に従って情報にアクセスします。

contents.html: With Role Based Access Control (RBAC), each role is associated with a set of operations which a user in that role may perform. The power of RBAC as an access control mechanism is the concept that an operation may theoretically be anything. This is contrasted to other access control mechanisms where bits or labels are associated with information blocks. These bits or labels indicate relatively simple operations, such as, read or write, which can be performed on an information block. Operations in RBAC may be arbitrarily complex, e.g., “a night surgical nurse can only append surgical information to a patient record from a workstation in the operating theater while on duty in that operating theater from midnight to 8 AM." A goal for implementing RBAC is to allow operations associated with roles to be as general as possible while not adversely impacting the administrative flexibility or the behavior of applications.
contents.html_ja: ロールベースアクセス制御（RBAC）では、各ロールに、そのロールのユーザーが実行できる一組の操作が関連付けられます。アクセス制御機構としての RBAC の強みは、操作が理論上は何であってもよいという考え方にあります。これは、情報ブロックにビットやラベルを関連付ける他のアクセス制御機構とは対照的です。それらのビットやラベルが示すのは、読み取りや書き込みなど、情報ブロックに対して実行できる比較的単純な操作です。RBAC の操作は、任意に複雑でもかまいません。たとえば「夜間の外科看護師は、手術室のワークステーションから、午前 0 時から午前 8 時まで当該手術室で勤務中に限り、患者記録に外科情報を追記できます」といったものです。RBAC を実装する際の目標は、ロールに関連付ける操作をできるだけ一般的なものにしながら、管理上の柔軟性やアプリケーションの動作に悪影響を与えないようにすることです。

contents.html: This approach has several advantages. One advantage is that applications need not change when access conditions for roles are changed. Applications use the methods of the application interface class whose methods have the same names, types, and parameters as the methods in the basic access methods class. The methods of the application interface class and the methods of the basic access methods class are fixed and remain constant over time. When access conditions for roles change, applications fail only because of access violations. This type of failure is comparable to the failures that typically occur when information protection bits or labels are changed. Applications are normally implemented to be able to handle access violations.
contents.html_ja: この方法にはいくつかの利点があります。1 つ目の利点は、ロールのアクセス条件が変更されても、アプリケーションを変更する必要がないことです。アプリケーションは、アプリケーションインターフェースクラスのメソッドを使い、そのメソッドは基本アクセスメソッドクラスのメソッドと同じ名前、型、パラメーターを持ちます。アプリケーションインターフェースクラスのメソッドと基本アクセスメソッドクラスのメソッドは固定されていて、時間が経っても変わりません。ロールのアクセス条件が変更されたとき、アプリケーションが失敗するのは、アクセス違反が生じたときだけです。この種の失敗は、情報保護ビットやラベルが変更されたときに通常起こる失敗に匹敵します。アプリケーションは通常、アクセス違反を処理できるように実装されています。

contents.html: Another advantage of this approach is that access conditions for roles are easily changed. Access conditions for roles are located exclusively within the role classes. Consequently, role policy changes do not require modifications to the applications themselves. One can conceive of a simple language, suitable for use by data and security administrators, for expressing access conditions restricted to conditionals and filters. A processor for such a language could generate the role objects and place them in the libraries used by applications. Most environments today support dynamically linked libraries which link when an application is loaded into memory for execution. Thus, applications do not need to be relinked when role classes are changed. This ability to easily change access conditions associated with roles permits rapid response to policy changes.
contents.html_ja: この方法のもう 1 つの利点は、ロールのアクセス条件を容易に変更できることです。ロールのアクセス条件は、ロールクラスの中にだけ置かれます。したがって、ロールのポリシーを変更しても、アプリケーション自体を修正する必要はありません。条件文とフィルターに限定したアクセス条件を表現するための、データ管理者やセキュリティ管理者が使うのに適した簡単な言語を考えることができます。そのような言語の処理系は、ロールオブジェクトを生成し、アプリケーションが使うライブラリに配置できるでしょう。現在のほとんどの環境は、アプリケーションが実行のためにメモリにロードされるときにリンクされる動的リンクライブラリをサポートしています。したがって、ロールクラスが変更されても、アプリケーションを再リンクする必要はありません。ロールに関連付けられたアクセス条件を容易に変更できるこの能力により、ポリシーの変更に迅速に対応できます。

contents.html: The demonstration illustrating the capabilities of each technology studied in the project consists of a distributed application for clinical and administrative patient data access. For this demo, a patient record data base object (PRDBO) is defined. This object provides a consistent view of the patient information. The concept is to access patient data through this object whose methods provide a consistent specification for accessing the data. How the data is actually stored is independent of how the object client accesses the data. The methods in the object implementation access the data however and wherever the data is actually stored. CORBA is being used as a means of implementing the PRDBO.
contents.html_ja: 本プロジェクトで調べた各技術の能力を示すデモンストレーションは、臨床および管理に関する患者データにアクセスするための分散アプリケーションで構成されます。このデモのために、患者記録データベースオブジェクト（PRDBO）を定義します。このオブジェクトは、患者情報の一貫したビューを提供します。考え方は、メソッドがデータにアクセスするための一貫した仕様を提供するこのオブジェクトを通じて、患者データにアクセスするというものです。データが実際にどのように格納されているかは、オブジェクトのクライアントがどのようにデータにアクセスするかとは無関係です。オブジェクト実装のメソッドは、データが実際に格納されているどこにあっても、どのような方法で格納されていてもアクセスします。PRDBO を実装する手段として CORBA を使用しています。

contents.html: The PRDBO organizes patient information into groups. Figure 9 shows the information groups of the PRDBO and how they relate to each other. The Identification Information Group contains information like name, address, and patient ID. The Demographic Information Group contains information like birth date and sex. The Encounter Information Group contains information like encounter date, physician seen, symptoms, and diagnosis. The Encounter Notes Group contains physician notes on the encounter. The Diagnostic Data Group contains the results of diagnostic procedures (e.g., X-rays) associated with the encounter. The Data Annotations Group contains annotations to the diagnostic data, such as, notations on an X-ray highlighting abnormalities. The Diagnostic Data and Data Annotations Groups usually contain multimedia information such as images and sound.
contents.html_ja: PRDBO は、患者情報をグループに編成します。図 9 は、PRDBO の情報グループと、それらが互いにどう関連しているかを示しています。識別情報グループには、氏名、住所、患者 ID などの情報が含まれます。人口統計情報グループには、生年月日や性別などの情報が含まれます。診察情報グループには、診察日、診察した医師、症状、診断などの情報が含まれます。診察メモグループには、診察に関する医師のメモが含まれます。診断データグループには、診察に関連する診断手順（たとえば X 線）の結果が含まれます。データ注釈グループには、診断データへの注釈が含まれ、たとえば X 線画像で異常を強調する書き込みなどです。診断データグループとデータ注釈グループには、通常、画像や音声などのマルチメディア情報が含まれます。

contents.html_ja: 医療デモンストレーションシステムは、分散型のクライアント／サーバーモデルに従っています。クライアントは、要求を含むメッセージをサーバーオブジェクトへ送ります。サーバーオブジェクトは要求を検証し、結果をメッセージでクライアントへ返します。
contents.html: The health care demonstration system follows a distributed, client-server model. Clients send messages containing requests to server objects. The server objects verify the request, and send results back to the client in messages.

contents.html_ja: クライアントとサーバーの通信に使うモデルは、オブジェクトベースです。クライアントは、患者記録データベースからデータを取り出すために、これらのオブジェクトにメッセージを送ります。クライアントから見ると、これらのオブジェクトはローカルにあります。クライアントは、実際のオブジェクト実装がネットワークの向こう側、場合によっては別のマシン上で動いていることを意識しません。
contents.html: The model used for client-server communication is object-based. Clients send messages to these objects in order to retrieve data from the patient record database. From the perspective of the client, these objects are local; the client is unaware that the actual object implementation is running across the network, possibly on a different machine.

contents.html_ja: サーバーオブジェクトは状態を保持しません。これらのオブジェクトは、患者記録データベースへの抽象的なインターフェースを提供するだけです。各メソッド呼び出しは独立しており、呼び出しの順序に定めはありません。サーバーオブジェクトは、患者記録データベースへのアクセスをカプセル化します。目標は、データベース、システム、ネットワークの変更にかかわらず、同じインターフェースを維持することです。
contents.html: The server objects retain no state. These objects only provide an abstract interface to the patient record database. Each method call is independent, and there is no prescribed ordering to the calling sequence. The server objects encapsulate the access to the patient record database. The goal is to maintain the same interface, independent of changes in databases, systems, or networks.

contents.html_ja: サーバーオブジェクトは状態を持たないため、すべてのアクセス制御は各メソッドによって実施されます。別のモデルでは、クライアントとサーバーオブジェクトの間のセッションという概念を使います。これは、サーバーオブジェクトに、要求者のユーザー ID などの何らかの状態を保持させることで実現できます。その場合、各メソッドは、適切なアクセスが許可されているかどうかを、その状態を調べて確認します。この手法では、他のメソッドよりも前に、あるメソッドを呼び出す必要があります。このメソッドは、要求者のロールに基づいてアクセス権限を確立します。（これは、オブジェクトのコンストラクターで行うことができます。）以降のメソッド呼び出しは、アクセスが許可済みであることを前提とします。
contents.html: Because the server objects are stateless, all access controls are enforced by each method. A different model would use the concept of sessions between the client and server objects. This can be accomplished by having the server objects retain some state, such as the user id if the requester. Each method then checks the state for the proper access being granted. This technique would require that one method be called before any others. This method would establish the access privileges based on the role of the requester. (This could be done by the object's constructor) Further method calls would assume that the access has been granted.

contents.html_ja: クライアントとサーバーオブジェクトの間のセッションという考え方を使う場合、サーバーオブジェクトがセッションを維持する方法は 2 つあります。1 つは、状態データの中にセッションの一覧を保持する、1 つのサーバーオブジェクトを置くことです。もう 1 つは、サーバーオブジェクトを 1 つのセッション専用にすることです。1 つ目の選択肢では、サーバーオブジェクトの実装を連続して動作させ、要求を受け付けてセッションを確立する必要があります。2 つ目の選択肢では、サーバーオブジェクトの存続期間はセッションの存続期間に限られます。
contents.html: By using the idea of a session between client and server object, we have two choices for server objects to maintain the session. One choice is to have one server object, which maintain lists of sessions in its state data. The other choice is to have the server object dedicated to one session only. The first option would require that the server object implementation run continuously, accepting requests and establishing sessions. In the second option, the lifetime of the server object is limited to the session lifetime.

contents.html_ja: Common Object Request Broker Architecture（CORBA）は、サーバーオブジェクトのインターフェースを、サーバーの実装とは独立に規定する手段を提供します。利点には、クライアントプログラムがサーバーの変更から独立していられること、およびサーバーとのインターフェースに一貫した手段が提供されることがあります。医療デモンストレーションの開発には、CORBA に準拠した製品を使用しました。
contents.html: The Common Object Request Broker Architecture (CORBA) provides a means to specify the interface for a server object independent of the server's implementation. The advantages include allowing the client programs to be independent of changes in the server, and a consistent means of interfacing to servers is provided. We have used a CORBA compliant product in the development of the health care demonstration.

contents.html_ja: クライアントプログラム（HTTP 用の CGIBIN スクリプトなど）は、患者記録データベースと直接通信しません。データベースへのインターフェースは、CORBA IDL（インターフェース定義言語）で規定されます。サーバープログラムは、データベースサーバーについて IDL で規定された操作を実装します。
contents.html: Client programs (such as the CGIBIN scripts for HTTP) do not communicate directly with the patient record database. The interface to the database is specified in CORBA IDL (interface definition language). A server program implements the operations specified in the IDL for the database server.

contents.html_ja: サーバー向けに開発したオブジェクトは、下位の患者記録データベースに対するラッパーを提供します。使用した IDL 言語は付録 B に示します。デモンストレーションプロジェクトでは、2 段階のラッパーを提供しています。第 1 段階は、データベースの各テーブルへの基本的なインターフェースを提供します。このインターフェースは patient_record_server_type と名付けられています。このインターフェースは、下位のデータベースの実装に従って、患者記録の一部を取り出すメソッドを提供します。各メソッドは、要求者のロールに基づいて情報へのアクセスを制御します。
contents.html: The objects developed for the server provide a wrapper to the underlying patient record database. The IDL language used is presented in Appendix B. There are two levels of wrappers provided in the demonstration project. The first level provides a basic interface to each of the database tables. This interface is named the patient_record_server_type. This interface provides methods to retrieve a piece of the patient record, as implemented by the underlying database. Each method provides controls on the access to the information based on the role of the requester.

contents.html: Each of the server methods has several responsibilities. The access controls are described below. Besides access control, the server methods must communicate with the patient record database. This communication is done via the Remote Database Access (RDA) architecture.
contents.html_ja: サーバーの各メソッドには、いくつかの責務があります。アクセス制御は以下で説明します。アクセス制御のほかに、サーバーのメソッドは、患者記録データベースと通信しなければなりません。この通信は、リモートデータベースアクセス（RDA）アーキテクチャを通じて行われます。

contents.html: The use of RDA allows for the server objects to connect to the database, no matter on what machine the database is located.
contents.html_ja: RDA を使うことで、サーバーオブジェクトは、データベースがどのマシン上にあっても、そのデータベースに接続できます。

contents.html: We now have two levels of independence in the demonstration project. The server objects do not depend on the location of the database, and the database access procedures. The interface to the database handles all necessary connections, such as locating the database on the network, and supplying commands and returning data.
contents.html_ja: これで、デモンストレーションプロジェクトには 2 段階の独立性があります。サーバーオブジェクトは、データベースの位置にも、データベースへのアクセス手順にも依存しません。データベースへのインターフェースは、ネットワーク上のデータベースの位置の特定、コマンドの供給、データの返却など、必要なすべての接続を扱います。

contents.html_ja: もう 1 つの段階の独立性は、クライアントとサーバーの間のものです。サーバーオブジェクトは、ネットワーク上のどのマシンでも動作させることができます（オブジェクトリクエストブローカーが存在することを前提とします）。クライアントプログラムはサーバーオブジェクトへメッセージを送り、下位のオブジェクトリクエストブローカー（ORB）が、そのメッセージを適切なサーバー実装へ配送します。さらに、動作しているサーバー実装がなければ、ORB に起動を指示できます。クライアントから見えるインターフェースは、メソッド呼び出しだけです。クライアントが、マシン名、ポート番号、その他の通信レベルの情報を知る必要はありません。このように、これらのメソッドは単なるリモートプロシージャコールにとどまらず、クライアントに対してより高い抽象化を提供します。
contents.html: The other level of independence is client to server. The server objects can be running on any machine on the network (presuming the existence of an object request broker). Client programs send messages to the server objects, and the underlying object request broker (ORB) delivers the messages to the appropriate server implementation. Furthermore, if there is no server implementation running, the ORB can be directed to start one. To the client, the only visible interface is that of method calls. There is no need for the client to know the machine name, port numbers, or other communication level information. In this way, the methods are more than remote procedure calls, and provide a higher abstraction for the clients.

contents.html: 4.1.2 Role-Based Access Control in the Server
contents.html_ja: 4.1.2 サーバーにおけるロールベースアクセス制御
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p37: 画像と語ごとに照合

contents.html: The assumption made by the server programs is that the clients are unable to do any form of role-based access control. Therefore, all access control is done by the servers. Access control is enforced by each method in the patient record server object. The user name, role, and password (encrypted) is sent to each method, along with the request for data. The user name/password combination is verified in the method. If the access check fails, no data is returned to the caller, and an error message is written into the access control block, which is returned.
contents.html_ja: サーバープログラムは、クライアントがいかなる形のロールベースアクセス制御も行えないことを前提としています。したがって、すべてのアクセス制御はサーバーが行います。アクセス制御は、患者記録サーバーオブジェクトの各メソッドによって実施されます。ユーザー名、ロール、（暗号化された）パスワードが、データの要求とともに各メソッドへ送られます。ユーザー名とパスワードの組み合わせは、メソッドの中で検証されます。アクセスチェックに失敗した場合は、呼び出し元へデータは返されず、エラーメッセージがアクセス制御ブロックに書き込まれて返されます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p37: ページ・行で分かれた断片を 1 つにし、画像と語ごとに照合

contents.html: If the access check is successful, the query on the database is performed. Before data is returned, any data items that are not accessible to the requester are eliminated from the data. This control allows pieces of the database tables to be accessed, while other pieces are suppressed. The server method uses a table-driven approach to remove any data not accessible because of the requester’s role.
contents.html_ja: アクセスチェックに成功した場合は、データベースに対する問い合わせが実行されます。データが返される前に、要求者がアクセスできないデータ項目はすべて、データから取り除かれます。この制御により、データベースのテーブルの一部にはアクセスでき、他の部分は抑止されます。サーバーのメソッドは、要求者のロールのためにアクセスできないデータを除去するのに、テーブル駆動の方法を使います。

contents.html: In the case of a patient requesting the entire patient record, the patient role server performs another form of verification. The request to the patient record server is made using the patient id as the criteria. The actual value of the id is retrieved from the verification database when the user-name/password check is made. The id value passed by the requester is not trusted, and is therefore not used.
contents.html_ja: 患者が患者記録全体を要求する場合は、患者ロールサーバーが別の形の検証を行います。患者記録サーバーへの要求は、患者 ID を条件として行われます。ID の実際の値は、ユーザー名とパスワードのチェックが行われるときに、検証用データベースから取得されます。要求者が渡した ID の値は信頼されないため、使用されません。

contents.html: The viewer was developed using the Multiple Document Interface (MDI). MDI is a standard method that allows an application to edit several documents of the same type simultaneously. The document controls the storage of the patient record as an OLE compound document. The document is implemented as the C++ class HealthDocument. The display of the data is done by the class HealthView that encapsulates the view. An external data record from the database is inserted using the code in figure 9. contents.html: Sockets were not implemented in the demo projects. A possible use was determined for them. Sockets are most useful for bulk communication while CORBA does poorly. The best use would be for large transfers, such as bitmaps, to be performed by connection oriented sockets. CORBA would be used to transmit the location of the bitmap to the CORBA client. The CORBA client would then make a connection to a file server on the host with the bitmap and retrieve the bitmap to the local machine. That way the CORBA layer is not responsible for transmission of the bitmap data itself.
contents.html_ja: ソケットは、デモプロジェクトでは実装しませんでした。使い道は想定されました。ソケットは大量通信に最も役立ち、CORBA はそれが不得手です。最適な使い方は、ビットマップなどの大きな転送をコネクション型のソケットで行うことでしょう。CORBA は、ビットマップの位置を CORBA クライアントに伝えるために使います。次に CORBA クライアントは、ビットマップを持つホスト上のファイルサーバーに接続し、ビットマップをローカルマシンへ取り出します。そうすれば、CORBA 層がビットマップのデータ自体の伝送を担うことはありません。

contents.html: In this report we have examined five distributed communication mechanisms. Table 5 presents our conclusions in tabular form. Each of the transport methods have different advantages and are best suited for different situations. Some are very specialized and are only good for certain tasks. SQL/RDA is an example of this type of method. It was designed to allow queries of remote databases. It does this task well but it does not support general communication. OLE does support communication between application, but best support is only provided in the Microsoft Windows environment. By limiting the environment this way, OLE can provide integration at the level of the user interface. Distributed COM will most likely be at the same level as CORBA.
contents.html_ja: 本報告書では、5 つの分散通信機構を検討しました。表 5 に、結論を表形式で示します。各トランスポート方式には異なる利点があり、最適な状況もそれぞれ異なります。非常に特化していて、特定のタスクにしか向かないものもあります。SQL/RDA はこの種の方式の例です。SQL/RDA はリモートのデータベースへの問い合わせを可能にするために設計されました。このタスクはうまくこなしますが、汎用の通信はサポートしません。OLE はアプリケーション間の通信をサポートしますが、最良のサポートが得られるのは Microsoft Windows 環境だけです。このように環境を限定することで、OLE はユーザーインターフェースのレベルでの統合を提供できます。分散 COM は、おそらく CORBA と同じレベルになるでしょう。

contents.html: The three general mechanisms trade efficiency for ease of use. The lowest level is the socket interface, which is very fast and efficient, but must be programmed at the lowest level. RPC is a higher level transport that also supplies a programming language independent IDL. The highest support is supplied by CORBA. A CORBA user can ask for an object and let the CORBA implementation worry about where the object can be found. The tradeoff is that communication using CORBA is inefficient.
contents.html_ja: 3 つの汎用機構は、効率と使いやすさのトレードオフの関係にあります。最も低いレベルはソケットインターフェースで、非常に高速で効率的ですが、最も低いレベルでプログラミングしなければなりません。RPC はより高いレベルのトランスポートで、プログラミング言語に依存しない IDL も提供します。最も高度なサポートを提供するのは CORBA です。CORBA の利用者は、オブジェクトを要求するだけで、そのオブジェクトがどこにあるかは CORBA 実装に任せられます。トレードオフとして、CORBA を使った通信は非効率です。

contents.html: In the demonstration viewers we attempted to show a way to use the various mechanisms to their best advantage. By combining the transport methods, we were able to get support when needed and efficiency when that was needed. Using each of the distributed transport mechanisms where it was most effective allowed us to achieve the best overall performance for the entire system. This is more complicated in terms of program development, but the payoffs can be quite high.

Abstract

The use of software in the health care industry is becoming of increasing importance. One of the major roadblocks to efficient health care is the fact that important information is distributed across many sites. These sites can be located across a significant area. The problem is to provide a uniform mechanism to integrate this information. This paper documents the results of an investigation into the suitability of several different distributed access mechanisms. Five methods were examined: the Common Object Request Broker (CORBA), Object Linking and Embedding (OLE), remote procedure call (RPC), remote database access (SQL/RDA) and Protocol Independent Interfaces (PH, we specifically examined sockets). These mechanisms were compared with regard for use in health care applications. In particular, the following
capabilities were compared:
Ease of use by the developer
Class of applications for which the technology is particularly effective in developing
Security capabilities
Protocols utilized
Performance of the transport mechanism.

A second goal was to explore the use of role-based access control (RBAC). RBAC is a security mechanism that is more flexible than Mandatory Access Control, but easier to use than just plain access control lists. Every user is assigned to one or more roles. Each role can perform
some operations but not others.

A demonstration application was constructed that used the distributed communication methods to implement a patient record database. This report discusses how these mechanisms were used in the demonstration project and the results found. Not unsurprisingly, we discovered that each of the mechanisms were effective for different purposes. These findings are discussed in detail in this report. One component of the demonstration project also implemented role-based
access control and is detailed in this report.

Introduction

Software is becoming of increasing importance in many industries, including the health care industry. An important characteristic of health care applications is that the data can be distributed across a wide area. Creating a comprehensive patient record can involve collecting information from many widely dispersed host machines. There are concerns about how fast large medical images can be transferred. There are also issues of how secure the data is when being
transferred over a private network.
The purpose of this report is to examine different transport mechanisms and to evaluate
We

their effectiveness in performing health care related tasks. selected five different transport mechanisms to examine: CORBA (Common Object Request Broker), OLE (Object Linking and Embedding), PE (Portable Independent Interfaces, specifically sockets), SQL/RDA (Remote Database Access) and RPC (Remote Procedure Call). Each of these were evaluated using five criteria:
How easy is it to use the product to develop applications?
What is the class of applications that the product is best suited to develop?
What are the security capabilities of the product?
What network transport protocols can be utilized?
What is the performance of the transport mechanism?
A

demonstration project was created in conjunction with this report. The goal of the demonstration project was to give an example of how the various communication technologies can be used in an actual application. We built two viewers of patient record data. One viewer was a POSIX (Portable Operating System Interface for Computer Environments, see [IEEE 1003.1c] and others) client that used a Hyper Text Markup Language (HTML) browser to examine patient data. The HTML browser found its data through a CORBA interface. The CORBA interface determined where the data of interest was located and queried the remote
database using SQL/RDA.

The second viewer used OLE. Since OLE is not yet a distributed mechanism, this viewer had a different function. The viewer was used to contain patient data that has already been collected from other sites into a patient report. Additional documents created by other applications could also be added to the patient report. For example, an article concerning new treatment taken from a medical journal could be incorporated. The viewer also had limited
ODBC
(Open Database

database querying ability. Local databases which support the Connectivity) protocol could be queried. This viewer was more limited than the previous viewer in the sense that it had to know the exact host on which the data resided. In this section of the report we have presented a general project overview. The next section will review each of the distributed communication methods and apply the evaluation criteria to each. After that is the section presenting a technical overview of role-based access control. The following section covers the demonstration project. Finally, we will present our conclusions.
Technical Overview of Transport Mechanisms
CORBA

CORBA, the Common Object Request Broker, provides integration of object systems within a client/server framework. Clients issue requests for services on objects and the server performs the requested service. The CORBA server is termed the "object implementation". The clients are isolated from the object implementation through commonly defined interfaces which specify the makeup and operations associated with each object and how the operations on the object are provided. Clients seamlessly access the object implementation wherever that object implementation may reside, i.e., in a library on the same host as the client, in another process on the same host as the client, or on a different host from the client where the two hosts are
connected by a network.

IDL is the language used for defining interfaces. IDL is programming language independent. When IDL is compiled, the output is programming language source code. Using IDL, the programmer describes the interfaces to the objects. The IDL compiler then takes the descriptions and outputs language in the target language. This code is a skeleton which the programmer then fills in. CORBA provides the Dynamic Invocation Interface which allows applications to generate requests at run-time. Target Language bindings are provided for C, C-M-, Ada and SmallTalk. The interfaces and methods of the IDL are mapped into programming constructs of the target language. For example, when DDL is mapped into C-H-, interfaces are mapped into classes and methods are mapped into functions, which perform the services of the interface. IDL does not specify how an interface is implemented. IDL does provide detailed information about the operations permitted on each object, the arguments expected, what is
returned, and what happens when errors occur.

Running an IDL script containing an interface definition through an IDL compiler generates the code for the client stubs and the implementation skeleton. Every possible operation on an object defined in the IDL generates a client stub. The client stubs bind the client to the object, i.e. translate between local and standard data representations, and marshal the method call parameters to and from the object. The implementation skeleton marshals the method call parameters to and from the client. The CORBA components and flow of information is shown in
figure 1.
CORBA
includes
an object model;
the Object Request Broker (ORB);
an object-oriented Interface Definition Language (IDL);
language mappings to the DDL (e.g., C C++, Smalltalk, Ada); ,
the mechanisms necessary for interoperability between clients and object implementations; and
standard services whose interfaces are defined in CORBA IDL.
Figure 1 . COREA Block Diagram
These standard services are used by clients and object implementations when interacting
CORBA
environment. Examples of standard services include the Interface Repository

with the which permits applications to get information about objects and their methods and Dynamic Invocation which permits applications to make requests to object implementations without having to be recompiled. CORBA is specified in three documents available from the Object Management Group (OMG): The Common Object Request Broker: Architecture and Specification (CORBA) [CORBASPEC], CORBAservices, and CORBAfacilities. The CORBA specification includes the object model, the semantics of the ORB, the DDL, the language mappings, interoperability, and basic object services. The CORBAservices specification includes additional services useful for realizing and maintaining objects within a distributed computing environment. These services include naming, events, lifecycle, persistence, transactions, concurrency, extemalization, and relationships. The CORBAfacilities specification includes both higher level services applicable across all application domains and higher level services targeted to specific application domains, such as manufacturing or healthcare. As new capabilities are developed, they are added to these documents. Currently under

SQL is a popular relational database language first standardized in 1986 by the American National Standards Institute (ANSI). Since then, it has been formally adopted as an International Standard by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC)[ISO9075]. It has also been adopted as a Federal Information
Processing Standard (FIPS) for the U.S. government.
The SQL standard is very popular with a large and increasing number of conforming implementations. It is, or soon will be, the basis of definition for a majority of Federal databases
and database applications involving structured data.

The basic structure of the relational model is a table, consisting of rows and columns. Data definition includes declaring the name of each table to be included in a database, the names and datatypes of all columns of each table, constraints on the values in and among columns, and the granting of table manipulation privileges to prospective users. Tables can be accessed by inserting new rows, deleting or updating existing rows, or selecting rows that satisfy a given search condition for output. Tables can be manipulated to produce new tables by Cartesian products, unions, intersections, joins on matching columns, or projections on given columns. The purpose of the SQL language standard is to provide portability of database definitions and database application programs among conforming implementations. Use of the SQL language standard is appropriate in all cases where there is to be some interchange of database information between systems. The SQL definition language may be used to interchange database definitions and application specific views. The SQL data manipulation language provides the data operations that make it possible to interchange complete application programs.

RPC, Remote Procedure Call, provides an application the ability to request services from other processes, usually remote, by means of a function call. The RPC concept is based on a client/server framework. The client application can execute a procedure on a local/remote machine, pass data to it and retrieve the result. When the machine is remote, RPC uses the
communication resources of the underlying network.

The two most widely used RPC implementations are ONC (Open Network Computing) RPC and DCE (Distributed Computing Environment) RPC. ONC/RPC, sometimes referred to as Sun/RPC, was developed by Sun Microsystems. ONC/RPC was one of the first commercial implementations of RPC. The success of ONC/RPC is in some measure related to the widespread use of NFS which is implemented using ONC/RPC. NFS has been implemented in many diverse
environments, e.g., IBM MVS, DEC VMS, and Novell Netware.
DCE/RPC was developed by the Open Software Foundation (OSF). The DCE/RPC protocol is used as an optional protocol in CORBA (see section 2.0). DCE/RPC is also the
COM
COM
protocol used by to extend functionality over a network (see section 2.1).

The basic operation of RPC is illustrated in figure 6. The paradigm of RPC is based on the concept of a function call in a programming language. The semantics of RPC are almost identical to the semantics of the traditional function call. The major difference is that while a normal procedure call takes place between procedures of a single process in the same memory space on a single system, RPC takes place between a client process on one system and a server process on another system where both the client system and the server system are connected to a
network.
A client application issues a normal function call to a client stub. The client stub receives arguments from and returns arguments to the calling function. An argument may instantiate an
input parameter, an output parameter or an input/output parameter.

The client stub converts the input arguments from the local data representation to a common data representation, creates a message containing the input arguments in their common data representation, and calls the client runtime, usually a library of routines that supports the functioning of the client stub. The client runtime transmits the message with the input arguments to the server runtime which is usually an object library that supports the functioning of the server stub. The server runtime issues a call to the server stub which takes the input arguments from the message, converts them from the common data representation to the local data representation of
the server, and calls the server application which does the processing.

When the server application has completed, it returns results to the server stub in the output arguments. The server stub converts the output arguments from the data representation of the server to the common data representation for transmission on the network and encapsulates the output arguments into a message which is passed to the server runtime. The server runtime transmits the message to the client runtime which passes the message to the client stub. Finally, the client stub extracts the arguments from the message and returns them to the calling procedure
in the required local data representation.

1 . no security 2. traditional process permission: uid, gid, supplementary groups, and machine name are provided 3. verification of identification provided (based on Diffie/Hellman key distribution DES encryption techniques).

and its aliases.

The methods of the application interface class also have the same names, types and parameters as the methods of the basic access methods class. The methods of the application interface class invoke the corresponding methods of the role classes. It is the methods of an application interface object which the application invokes. Given the current role associated with the application, the methods of the application interface object select the appropriate role object. This approach has several advantages. One advantage is that applications need not change when access conditions for roles are changed. Applications use the methods of the application interface class whose methods have the same names, types, and parameters as the methods in the basic access methods class. The methods of the application interface class and the methods of the basic access methods class are fixed and remain constant over time. When access conditions for roles change, applications fail only because of access violations. This type of failure is comparable to the failures that typically occur when information protection bits or labels are changed. Applications are normally implemented to be able to handle access
violations.

Another advantage of this approach is that access conditions for roles are easily changed. Access conditions for roles are located exclusively within the role classes. Consequently, role policy changes do not require modifications to the applications themselves. POSIXDemo 4.1 The health care demonstration system follows a distributed, client-server model. Clients send messages containing requests to server objects. The server objects verify the request, and send results back to the client in messages. The model used for client-server communication is object-based. Clients send messages to these objects in order to retrieve data from the patient record database. From the perspective of the client, these objects are local; the client is unaware that the actual object implementation is running across the network, possibly on a different machine. The server objects retain no state. These objects only provide an abstract interface to the patient record database. Each method call is independent, and there is no prescribed ordering to the calling sequence. The server objects encapsulate the access to the patient record database. The goal is to maintain the same interface, independent of changes in databases, systems, or networks. Because the server objects are stateless, all access controls are enforced by each method. A different model would use the concept of sessions between the client and server objects. This can be accomplished by having the server objects retain some state, such as the user id if the requester. Each method then checks the state for the proper access being granted. This technique would require that one method be called before any others. This method would establish the access privileges based on the role of the requester. (This could be done by the object's constructor) Further method calls would assume that the access has been granted. By using the idea of a session between client and server object, we have two choices for server objects to maintain the session. One choice is to have one server object, which maintain lists of sessions in its state data. The other choice is to have the server object dedicated to one session only. The first option would require that the server object implementation mn continuously, accepting requests and establishing sessions. In the second option, the lifetime of the server object is limited to the session lifetime. The Common Object Request Broker Architecture (CORBA) provides a means to specify the interface for a server object independent of the server's implementation. The advantages include allowing the client programs to be independent of changes in the server, and a consistent means of interfacing to servers is provided. We have used a CORBA compliant product in the development of the health care demonstration. Client programs (such as the CGIBIN scripts for HTTP) do not communicate directly with the patient record database. The interface to the database is specified in CORBA IDL (interface definition language). A server program implements the operations specified in the DDL for the database server. The objects developed for the server provide a wrapper to the underlying patient record database. The DDL language used is presented in Appendix B. There are two levels of wrappers provided in the demonstration project. The first level provides a basic interface to each of the database tables. 4.1.1 Operation of the server object methods
Each of the server methods has several responsibilities. The access controls are described below. Besides access control, the server methods must communicate with the patient record

RDA

The use of allows for the server objects to connect to the database, no matter on what machine the database is located. We now have two levels of independence in the demonstration project. The server objects do not depend on the location of the database, and the database access procedures. The interface to the database handles all necessary connections, such as locating the database on the network, and supplying commands and returning data. The other level of independence is client to server. The server objects can be running on any machine on the network (presuming the existence of an object request broker). Client programs send messages to the server objects, and the underlying object request broker (ORB) delivers the messages to the appropriate server implementation. Furthermore, if there is no server implementation running, the ORB can be directed to start one. To the client, the only visible interface is that of method calls. There is no need for the client to know the machine name, port numbers, or other communication level information. In this way, the methods are more than remote procedure calls, and provide a higher abstraction for the clients.
4.1.2 Role-Based Access Control in the Server

The assumption made by the server programs is that the clients are unable to do any form of role-based access control. Therefore, all access control is done by the servers. Access control is enforced by each method in the patient record server object. The user name, role, and password (encrypted) is sent to each method, along with the request for data. The user name/password combination is verified in the method. If the access check fails, no data is returned to the caller, and an error message is written into the access control block, which is
returned.

If the access check is successful, the query on the database is performed. Before data is returned, any data items that are not accessible to the requester are eliminated from the data. This control allows pieces of the database tables to be accessed, while other pieces are suppressed. The server method uses a table-driven approach to remove any data not accessible
because of the requester’s role.

In the case of a patient requesting the entire patient record, the patient role server performs another form of verification. The request to the patient record server is made using the patient id as the criteria. The actual value of the id is retrieved from the verification database when the user-name/password check is made. The id value passed by the requester is not trusted,
and is therefore not used.

Conclusions

In this report we have examined five distributed communication mechanisms. Table 5 presents our conclusions in tabular form. Each of the transport methods have different advantages and are best suited for different situations. Some are very specialized and are only good for certain tasks. SQL/RDA is an example of this type of method. It was designed to allow queries of remote databases. It does this task well but it does not support general communication. OLE does support communication between application, but best support is only provided in the Microsoft Windows environment. By limiting the environment this way, OLE

original_blocks.html: There are three basic services supplied by COM: persistent storage, intelligent names and Uniform Data Transfer. Persistent Storage is the ability to store the state data of COM Objects so that they can be deleted and later restored. Intelligent names not only name a COM Object, but also contain information on how to reference the contents of the object. Uniform data transfer allows two applications to exchange data without the applications understanding the internals of each other.

original_blocks.html: When the server application has completed, it returns results to the server stub in the output arguments. The server stub converts the output arguments from the data representation of the server to the common data representation for transmission on the network and encapsulates the output arguments into a message which is passed to the server runtime. The server runtime transmits the message to the client runtime which passes the message to the client stub. Finally, the client stub extracts the arguments from the message and returns them to the calling procedure in the required local data representation.

original_blocks.html: The viewer was developed using the Multiple Document Interface (MDI). MDI is a standard method that allows an application to edit several documents of the same type simultaneously. Each document has its own main window that is enclosed by the main window of the application. Each document window can be minimized or have its size changed independently. The viewer also uses the Doc/View model where the contents of the document are separated from the way the contents are displayed. This makes the display of embedded OLE objects easier. The document controls the storage of the patient record as an OLE compound document. The document is implemented as the C++ class HealthDocument. The display of the data is done by the class HealthView that encapsulates the view. An external data record from the database is inserted using the code in figure 9. All redrawing of the window and other GUI activities are handled by the OWL and OCF library code.
